title: YEAR STACK
rule: the scroll is time; one sentence at the top says what was true in the year under it
description: Six years as six big cards, newest first, stacked as a pile with 2026 on top. A sticky sentence at the top, 'Gentrit Rashiti builds a multi-tenant platform, from the design system to the API behind it.', rewrites to the year of the card under it once the newer card's link has gone under it. Each card names two or three decisions with their results and pins one result to the pixel that proves it. Results with no screen close the page as four rows in 'Also on the record'.
signature: Gentrit Display (Hubot Sans) for the statement and Gentrit Text (Mona Sans) for text, the 160 px year numerals and the 14 px year links, on white, with one butter and navy identity: the current year's card is the butter panel, everything else is navy on white. Desktop: the statement is three lines, one clause on each, 'Gentrit Rashiti builds' opens the first; the six year links sit at its right on the last line. When a year earlier than 2026 settles (160 ms after the scroll stops on it), the 2026 words of each clause are struck (260 ms) and that year's words write in after them one whole word at a time (140 ms opacity each, stagger up to 60 ms, 320 ms in all, 30 ms line stagger), so no frame shows a cut glyph. The edit ends its line, so no other word moves; leaving words fade (120 ms) before they give up their width. The stack is in true order: all six cards stick from the first frame, the newer one on top and each older one 24 px lower (the step shrinks to 12 px on screens 840 px tall or less), so the first screen shows a pile of six whose last edge sits at y 880 of a 900 px screen. Scroll lifts the newer card off with native scroll and shows the older card under it, still and whole; nothing scales or dims. Each slot holds a 72 px dwell plus one step for each card above it, so every card shows whole and still for the same 64 px of scroll after the newer card has gone under the statement, and a card becomes current only when the newer card's link has gone under the statement. Each card's first result draws a navy hairline (180 ms, then a 120 ms outline) the first time the card is current; the line runs through the gap between the text and the plate, enters the plate from its left edge along a rule or a clear row, and ends at the part: the organization switcher on the live care recreation (along the plate's own divider), the store badges on bayyinah.org, Passkey on the Incentiv sign-in, the plan switch on Bayyinah TV pricing, a book row with progress on Read to Feed, the search field on Dukagjini Bookstore. Inside a dark plate the line is butter. Every plate ends on a whole row; the store listings are one screen each, cropped inside the phone frame, flush to the card's right edge, and their decisions take the width the listing leaves (the first row across, the others in two columns). The 2022 card holds three decisions: the reader, the React Native upgrades, and the chatbot runtime package. After the stack, 'Also on the record' holds four rows (year, project, decision, result): the 16 → 2 billing report, Offday's 16 isolation tests, Snaxx Tech's 972 → 337 KB, and the care platform's Vue years in four languages. The year links and arrow keys jump with no travel; a covered card that takes focus comes to the top with no travel. Phone: cards do not stick; the sentence uses the desktop width (108%) at 15 px in three lines: the name and the struck first clause on line one, the year's whole sentence on the two lines under it (92 px header). Reduced motion: the pile stays (position is not motion), the sentence and hairlines switch with no transition.
holdback: Lowest: original, 7/10. A sticky card stack with a sentence that reacts to the current card is the loop's house style; polish cannot move that point. Known limits: every desktop card is 620 px tall for about 460 px of content, so each card keeps 80 to 120 px of butter above its link; the deeper cards stick lower, so at 2021 the band between the statement and the card is 128 px of white; the phone statement is 15 px (it is 108% wide like the desktop, so the name and the struck clause need the smaller size to stay on one line at 343 px).
